title: Soil Temperature Source Inventory and Authority Pin

production_context.note: Read-only context pin. Any later implementation must resolve the then-current canonical authority again.

current_process_hydraulic_view.temperature_target_rule: Consume a process-facing hydraulic/water-content view. Do not import HeadCalc or soil-water solver internals.

legacy_archive_pin.note: The current canonical repository snapshot does not contain the full legacy soil-temperature source. This archive is therefore pinned as the audited legacy source artifact for readiness evidence, not as production source authority.

legacy_files.role: MOD_SoilTemperature, analytic and numerical soil-temperature formulations, De Vries thermal properties and thermal boundary input
MOD_frost, temperature-derived hydraulic reduction factors and frozen drainage/bottom-boundary modification
Legacy process ordering and temporal cadence
Restart serialization evidence: TSOIL is written/read when SWHEA > 0
Root-uptake and oxygen/frost consumers of soil temperature
Crop development/sowing consumer of soil temperature

source_bound_findings.numeric_cadence: SoilTemperature(2) is called after the accepted SoilWater loop on each successful model timestep, before solute and final time advancement. It is not intrinsically daily.
source_bound_findings.analytic_cadence: The analytic profile is materialized when SoilTemperature is called but is a function of integer daynr and depth, creating a legacy calendar-day dependency that must not become a kernel time-unit assumption.
source_bound_findings.numeric_persistent_state: tsoil(1:numnod) is the continuation state. On swinco=3, numerical initialization preserves the restored profile.
source_bound_findings.restart_evidence: swapoutput serializes TSOIL when SWHEA > 0. Frost reduction arrays/depths are not serialized and are recomputable from temperature plus current hydraulic/configuration inputs.
source_bound_findings.water_dependency: Numerical thermal properties use the average of current and previous volumetric water content, 0.5*(theta+thetm1).
source_bound_findings.snow_dependency: When snow storage is present, the top soil boundary temperature is derived from air temperature, top-node temperature and snow thermal resistance.
source_bound_findings.ice_dependency: No explicit ice-content state or latent-heat term was found in MOD_SoilTemperature. Legacy frost effects are applied separately as hydraulic reductions.
source_bound_findings.frost_ownership: MOD_frost is a separate process family. It consumes tsoil/tetop and modifies hydraulic conductivity, drainage and bottom flux. It currently imports hydraulic/drainage internals and therefore needs a separate migration boundary rather than being absorbed into the soil-temperature owner.
source_bound_findings.energy_accounting: The numerical conduction solve uses heat capacity, conductivity and top/bottom boundary terms but no explicit persistent/cumulative energy ledger was found. Energy-balance qualification therefore remains a child task before production implementation.
